memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Any fabric, woven or knitted material, or any leather article that has been washed and is rid of the mould, must be washed again. Then it will be clean." - Lev 13:58 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Washed, cleared, and then washed again. And this time the verdict is unqualified: then it will be clean.

The whole long chapter has been building to sentences like this one. Amid all the examining and isolating and burning, again and again God provides a route back. Cleanness was always the goal. Exclusion was never the point.

Notice also what happens to the garment. It goes back into use. It is not kept in a cupboard as a memorial to what once grew in it. Someone wears it again, and it does the job it was made for.

That is what God does with restored people. Peter denied Jesus three times, publicly and shamefully. And the risen Christ took him aside, restored him three times over, and gave him work to do: feed my sheep (John 21:17). Not sidelined. Not permanently marked. Commissioned.

Paul called himself the worst of sinners, and then said God showed him mercy precisely so that Christ might display His immense patience as an example for those who would believe (1 Tim 1:16).

If God has cleansed you, He has not finished with you. He intends to use you. The washing was never so you could sit safely in a cupboard.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you believe God still has purpose for you after your failures?
2. Have you taken yourself out of service because of your past?
3. What work might God be calling you back into?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that You cleanse and then commission. Do not let me sideline myself over what You have already washed away — put me back to work for You. Amen.
